lines.text: This is a ravine. And this is a pizza.
With a little physics, my robot will fly it across and land it right here.
But first, we need to rewind a bit.
My buddy Theo lives across that ravine.
As the crow flies, a hundred and fifty meters. Driving around? Four kilometers.
So here's the plan. We string a rope from my deck to his treehouse.
The robot hooks on, and two motors drive it across at four meters per second.
Near the end, a sensor spots a reflector, it brakes, and a winch lowers the pizza onto his deck.
Then it zips home for the next order.
I designed it in CAD, sensor angled to catch the reflector ten meters out.
But here's what almost wrecked everything.
Robot plus pizza is about ten kilograms. That's ninety-eight newtons pulling down.
But the rope only sags three meters, and a rope that flat has to pull way harder to hold it up.
Each end gets yanked with over twelve hundred newtons. Like two adults hanging off it!
Which explains why attempt one ended up in the creek.
